source_text: Klagel. Jerem. 4, 19. Ἰστορεῖ γὰρ Ἰώσηππος ὡς οὐδὲ τὰ ὄρη τοὺς φεύγοντας διέσωσεν. ἐκεῖ τοίνυν ἡμᾶς ἕλκοντες ἥπτοντο, ἤγουν πρὸς δίκην ἀνήφθησαν καθ’ ἡμῶν. νοοῖτο δ’ ἂν καὶ περὶ τῶν ἀποστόλων ὧν >ἀνεκαινίσθη ὡς ἀετοῦ ἡ νεότης<.
pass_a_gloss: [Pass A] For Josephus narrates that not even the mountains saved those fleeing. There, then, dragging us they were fastening, or rather toward judgment they were kindled against us. And it would also be understood about the apostles whose “youth was renewed as an eagle’s.”
pass_b_english: For Josephus narrates that not even the mountains saved those fleeing. There, then, dragging us they were fastening, or rather toward judgment they were kindled against us. And it would also be understood about the apostles whose “youth was renewed as an eagle’s.” (Lamentations 4:19) (Psalm 103:5)

choices.why: 2 Cor 3 veil reading of Lam 4:20 ‘spirit of our face’.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Origen’s Greek Lamentations fragments. Sense checked against Klostermann GCS III. Modern English not copied. OET = no previous English translation.
